32.0.0.en: 1 So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes. 2 Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God. 3 Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job. 4 Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he. 5 When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was kindled.

32.0.1.en: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes [1].

32.0.2.en: The three friends stopped speaking, either because they saw God Himself defending Job as righteous, or because Job counted himself righteous, so that there was no profit in debating with him. The real fact is that they failed to prove their accusations against Job because they carried in their hearts and thoughts an insincere intention, so their accusations had no weight.

32.0.3.en: "Because he was righteous in his own eyes": this text reads in the Septuagint, the Syriac, the old Arabic and the Chaldean, "because he was righteous in their eyes." They were convinced that he was righteous and that their accusations had no basis.

32.0.4.en: The text reads in the translation of Symmachus, "because he appeared more righteous than they."

32.0.5.en: In the previous chapters we saw that Job did not deny that he had sins, and that he confessed them; but he was suffering because of what had befallen him, which had disfigured his image and caused his friends to stumble over him.

32.0.6.en: * They had no answer to this (that is, to what Job said), so Job fell silent to give them the word. And since he had received testimony from God (that he was blameless), they shut their mouths.

32.0.7.en: [Because Job was righteous before them]... They changed their former opinion, for by speaking against Job they condemn God. Note that in both cases there is a lack of proportion. They condemned Job as they did God also, and testified against both. But God did not defend Himself; rather He defended Job, ignoring the defense of Himself. He drew all eyes to him (Job 1:8), and He also said of Job: [You have not spoken of Me what is right, as My servant Job has] (see 42:8). In all this God bore the utmost degree of injustice.

32.0.8.en: St. John Chrysostom God, in His love for His believers, defends them, whether as individuals or as a community. The psalmist says: "I cry... to God who defends me" (Ps 57:2). "The Lord will defend me. O Lord, thy mercy endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands" (Ps 138:8). As for the community, it is said: "For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake" (Isa 37:35; 38:6; Zech 9:15).

32.0.9.en: In the midst of the accusations of those nearest to us, we lift our eyes to our Lord Jesus, as the fortress in which we take refuge, the refuge of our salvation and our defender.

32.0.10.en: * [You have become my hope, and a tower in the face of the enemy] (Ps 61:3). He says: My heart is troubled, for they have gathered together from the ends of the earth, and I have come to suffer in the midst of trials and attack... Inside the Church the wheat suffers from the violence of the chaff. In the midst of all these things, since my heart is troubled, I cry out from the ends of the earth.. Christ Himself is the tower. He makes Himself a tower from the face of the enemy, and He is also the rock on which the Church is built. Do you wish not to be struck by Satan? Flee to the tower. The arrows of Satan will not be able to weary you in that tower. There you take shelter and stand firm... The tower is before you. Call Christ to your minds, and enter the tower!

32.0.11.en: St. Augustine Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram.

32.1.0.en: Against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God [2].

32.1.1.en: "Elihu" is a Hebrew name meaning "He is my God." The wrath here indicates his inner emotion and his great zeal to defend God's justice, His righteousness and His care.

32.1.2.en: * [Against Job was his wrath kindled, because he counted himself righteous before God] [2]. Elihu was angry, not because Job declared that he was righteous, but because he did this before the Lord, whom he counted as a witness, or he thought that Job wanted to condemn God. His justifying himself was of no importance; but to do so with the purpose of condemning God is wrong. Scripture says: [Justify not thyself before the Lord] (Sir 7:5)...

32.1.3.en: Did this happen? Job's thought was not so. It was Elihu who understood it in this way; Job did not say that he was more righteous than God, but rather his thought was that God was responsible for his calamities. Even so, he did not wrong God by accusing Him of injustice; this is only what Elihu understood.

32.1.4.en: St. John Chrysostom "Elihu," or "He is Jehovah, God." His name and his character announce his role as a messenger between God and Job, preparing Job to enjoy the vision of God coming in the whirlwind. He bore a shadow of the true Mediator, our Lord Jesus (Job 33:23-26).

32.1.5.en: Barachel: it means "God blesses." The name of Elihu and the name of his father indicate that this family was marked by godliness and did not practice idol worship.

32.1.6.en: The Buzite: Buz was the second son of Nahor, the brother of Abraham (Gen 22:21), and this region in the Arabian desert was called by his name; the name of the city of Buz occurs in (Jer 25:23); perhaps it took its name from the family. Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that the word "Buzite" is translated "contemptible."

32.1.7.en: Some rabbis and St. Jerome hold that Elihu is Balaam the son of Beor. Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that Elihu, as an example of arrogant preachers, offers us an interpretation of his name, the name of his father and the name of his kindred: for although they do not live according to the commandments of the Lord, they know God as their Lord. And while they enjoy the blessing of divine grace in the eloquence of their speech, in their arrogant conduct they show that they are despised. Dr. Hodges holds that Elihu is one of the appearances of the Second Hypostasis, and that the aim of the whole book is to focus on the person of Elihu and to bring out his role in convincing Job that his justification does not rest on reliance on his good works and clinging to his own righteousness, but on faith in the One who is able to justify.

32.1.8.en: None of the Fathers of the Church has proclaimed this opinion, but it may be said that he was a type of the Lord Christ, who comes to accomplish mediation and reconciliation, and so justifies the believers who walk in Him in spirit and truth.

32.1.9.en: Ram: Ram - Aram was the nephew of Buz, and perhaps Job was of a generation earlier than Elihu, since he was older than he. Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that the word "Ram" means "exalted." True believers are exalted, for they can say with the Apostle Paul: [For our conversation is in heaven] (Phil 3:20).

32.1.10.en: "Because he justified himself rather than God": perhaps he means "because he counted himself righteous before God." The literal translation is: "he justified his soul before God." He defended not only his conduct, but also his thoughts and inner motives.

32.1.11.en: Elihu differed from the three friends as to the intention of the two parties, for Elihu bore no malice or envy toward Job like these friends. On the other hand, he did not accuse him of committing grave hidden evils or of being a hypocrite; what he criticized in him was that in his speech he did not justify God, but what occupied him was justifying himself before God as well as before men, even if he feared that they would stumble over him as a man of God.

32.2.0.en: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job [3].

32.2.1.en: They had condemned Job, but they were unable to answer his arguments in general, and his justification of himself. Truly they sat silent, but they did not change their thoughts about him, and at the same time they failed to answer him.

32.2.2.en: What Job's friends did wrong was that they lacked a spirit of compassion toward a man who was tried and suffering like Job. They accused him of hypocrisy and of being wicked, and though unable to prove it, they did not wish to retreat. They reached a conclusion and a verdict on a man beforehand, before conversing with him, and their dialogue had no aim except to crush him completely.

32.2.3.en: Perhaps among the wonderful traits of Elihu is that, though his heart was filled with compassion for Job, as a mediator between the two parties he did not take a position of favoritism toward Job at the expense of his friends, but with gentleness and prudence he brought out the error of both parties. He began with Job so as to give the friends the opportunity to receive his words seriously and to reassess their dialogue with Job.

32.3.0.en: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he [4].

32.3.1.en: Elihu waited until the elders were silent and stopped speaking. By waiting he showed the wisdom of the elders while still a young man; he kept silent when they spoke, not because they were wiser than he, but because they were older than he. He kept to good order and fitting management, and when they fell silent in failure, while insisting on what was in their minds, he spoke with the spirit of truth, with boldness and prudence. Holy Scripture has commanded honoring the elders, but in the Lord:

32.3.2.en: "Despise not a man in his old age: for even some of us wax old" (Sir 8:7).

32.3.3.en: "Rebuke not an elder, but entreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren" (1 Tim 5:1).

32.3.4.en: "Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses" (1 Tim 5:19).

32.4.0.en: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was kindled [5].

32.4.1.en: Elihu was jealous for the Lord, for Job had sinned by not leaving the matter to God, counting that an injustice had been done to him. And Elihu regarded the silence of the three elders as a kind of consent and agreement with Job's opinion, so he was jealous for the glory and wisdom of the Lord.

32.5.0.en: 6 And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion. 7 I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom. 8 But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding. 9 Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment. 10 Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will shew mine opinion.

32.5.1.en: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said:

32.5.2.en: I am young, and ye are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion [6].

32.5.3.en: In ancient times, especially in the region of Asia, the young were not permitted to enter into dialogue with those older than themselves; sometimes the young man kept silent as far as possible on any subject.

32.5.4.en: His saying, "I am young in days," is an expression indicating a difference in age, whatever its extent; it may also indicate that he has less experience across the days because of his young age, but it does not mean he is less than they in wisdom.

32.6.0.en: I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom [7].

32.6.1.en: Elihu holds that wisdom does not depend on the mere experience of years. We can distinguish three kinds of wisdom:

32.6.2.en: Wisdom acquired through the experience of life; this grows with the years, and the elders hold it dear.

32.7.0.en: And wisdom as a natural gift which God has given to man in general, since He gave them reason by nature [8]. Often some of our children are wiser and more intelligent than we, even if they do not enjoy the same experience as ours.

32.7.1.en: And finally wisdom is the gift of the Spirit of God, which He gives to His godly ones.

32.7.2.en: While we hold dear and esteem the first two kinds of wisdom, the surpassing wisdom of God remains the object of our continual asking of God. [Give me wisdom, that sitteth by thy throne; and reject me not from among thy children] (Wis 9:4).

32.7.3.en: * All this wisdom and prudence are found in Christ, and through Christ we understand God (the Father) and see Him; so whatever wisdom remains in the world, any wisdom of this kind outside Christ and without Him is counted vain, worthless and base.

32.7.4.en: Fr. Marius Victorinus * Solomon says in Ecclesiastes that the eyes of the wise man are in his head (Eccl 2:14). Paul understood the importance of headship. He knew why the eyes are in the head. If Christ is the head of the believer, and the eyes of the wise man are in the head, then all our senses, our mind, our thought, our speech and our counsel (if we are wise) will be in Christ.

32.7.5.en: St. Jerome But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding [8].

32.7.6.en: The Hebrew text is translated literally "the Spirit Himself," meaning that man is given the Spirit, the giver of wisdom, or the spirit of inspiration. Elihu had earlier honored the elders for their experience; now he brings out that wisdom is a gift of God, which the old man can enjoy as the young man can. True wisdom, though it does not ignore experience through life, is fundamentally an inspiration from the Almighty, or a breath from the Almighty, "nishmat Shaday."

32.7.7.en: Some hold that the word "spirit" here refers to the breath which God gave to man (Gen 2:7), which gives him understanding.

32.8.0.en: Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment [9].

32.8.1.en: With the multitude of days a man may gain useful experience, whether in his own life or in the lives of others whom he meets and deals with; he may also gather many proverbs full of wisdom and memorize some of them by heart, and yet he may not practice wisdom, nor enjoy the spirit of discernment and understanding.

32.8.2.en: This is the argument by which Elihu justifies his position, that he has intruded into the situation to speak among elders, and to point out to them some judgments and counsels, and even to rebuke them.

32.8.3.en: Some hold that he is speaking of the wisdom granted by God, since He gave man the breath of a rational life. "Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it" (Eccl 12:7). "Thus saith the Lord, which stretcheth forth the heavens, and layeth the foundation of the earth, and formeth the spirit of man within him" (Zech 12:1).

32.8.4.en: Therefore I said, Hearken to me.

32.9.0.en: I also will shew mine opinion [10].

32.9.1.en: Elihu asks the elders not to despise him because of his young age, but rather to listen to him first and then examine his words.

32.9.2.en: It is fitting for us not to look lightly on those younger than ourselves, but to listen to them. The wise man says: [Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king] (Eccl 4:13).

32.10.s.en: 3. With patience he bore what had been said

32.10.0.en: 11 Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say. 12 Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, there was none of you that convinced Job, or that answered his words: 13 Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.

32.10.1.en: Behold, I waited for your words.

32.10.2.en: I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say [11].

32.10.3.en: It is as though he says to them: "I was listening to your words and attending to your arguments, and I found you lovers of disputation, searching for bare words here and there; and all that concerned you in the matter was to find words, whatever they might be, to carry out what was within you toward Job, rather than to touch the truth and offer love. By this he accuses you of your manner of dialogue. It is the manner of one who wants to win and excel with words, not of one who builds up himself and others. What occupied them throughout their whole dialogue was to contend with Job, and here they have failed in their barren contention.

32.10.4.en: * When you meet a man who loves disputes, and he begins to argue with you about what is self-evident and true, cut off the conversation and withdraw quickly, for his mind has turned to stone.

32.10.5.en: For as water spoils the finest wines, so foolish discussions spoil the virtuous in their conduct and in their characters.

32.10.6.en: St. Anthony the Great * Always flee from every man who does not cease from argument in his speech.

32.10.7.en: * If the soul withdraws from all discussion, disturbance and agitation, then the Spirit of God enters into it, and that which was barren becomes fruitful.

32.11.0.en: Abba Poemen Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, there was none of you that convinced Job, or that answered his words [12].

32.11.1.en: He made clear their failure in the dialogue, for they were unable to persuade Job's mind and change it, and they also failed to give convincing answers to his questions. They uttered a huge quantity of words, which were powerless to remove what was in Job's mind.

32.11.2.en: Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom.

32.12.0.en: God thrusteth him down, not man [13].

32.12.1.en: Here Elihu brings out what lay behind their dialogue and discussions, for they supposed in themselves that they were able to convince him by their own wisdom, whereas man needs an inner conviction coming from God, who alone overcomes the mind and subdues it, a thing of which man is incapable, whatever his linguistic and philosophical abilities.

32.12.2.en: God did not allow them victory in their dialogue, lest they rely on their own wisdom.

32.13.s.en: 4. His inner depths impel him to intervene

32.13.0.en: 14 Now he hath not directed his words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches. 15 They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking. 16 When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still, and answered no more;) 17 I said, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion. 18 For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me. 19 Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles. 20 I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer. 21 Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man. 22 For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.

32.13.1.en: Now he hath not directed his words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches [14].

32.13.2.en: Elihu says: [I am not a party to the dialogue, for Job has not uttered a single word against me; therefore my speech carries no emotions and does not issue from inward agitation, but springs from the desire for the truth. At the same time I will not speak to him in your manner, full of violence and harshness, which bore a folly that came out of your mouths. So, without partiality and without bias, I speak with him and also with you].

32.14.1.en: It seems that he turned his gaze to those present and began to speak with them about the position of the three friends, how they were bewildered and could not answer a word, for they felt that their words were worthless babble.

32.14.2.en: "Good" holds that the talk here is not about the friends, but about their words, which no longer carried any effectiveness, going out of their mouths to be dissipated in the air, carrying no meaning and offering nothing new.

32.14.3.en: When I had waited, (for they spake not.

32.15.0.en: But stood still, and answered no more;) [16].

32.15.1.en: Elihu says that he was waiting for the friends to utter a word and answer Job, and since they had become mute, he came forward to speak.

32.15.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees in Job's friends a type of the heretics who stir up many disputes, accuse the Church and resist her, but in the end the Lord upholds His Church and silences the heretics.

32.16.0.en: I said, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion [17].

32.16.1.en: The time had come for Elihu's turn. Now he became like one receiving his portion, by revealing the knowledge that he had kept hidden throughout the dialogue that went on between Job and the friends. He counted this as his portion, which came to him as a gracious gift offered to him.

32.16.2.en: Some hold that his saying, "I also will shew mine opinion," carries in the Hebrew original a touch of gentleness and humility that does not appear clearly in translations into other languages. It is as though he says: [Even I, the young man, a humble man like me, am permitted to express my opinions, while the elders and the great have nothing left to say].

32.16.3.en: For I am full of matter.

32.17.0.en: The spirit within me constraineth me [18].

32.17.1.en: The true believer bears a fiery spirit, in the likeness of God the consuming fire, or a fire of love that is not quenched (Ex 24:17; Deut 4:24; Heb 12:29), and so he becomes like one of the servants of God of whom it is said: "His ministers a flame of fire" (Heb 1:7).

32.17.2.en: The believer carries the word of God - the blazing fire of love - and so becomes like our teacher the Apostle Paul, who was "pressed in the spirit" (Acts 18:5), full of blazing spiritual zeal, who says: "For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ" (2 Cor 11:2). And he cries out with the prophet Jeremiah: "My bowels, my bowels! I am pained at my very heart... I cannot hold my peace" (Jer 4:19), "Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay" (Jer 20:9).

32.17.3.en: So Elihu felt like one constrained by the Spirit of God, who kindles the fires of his love toward Job as toward his friends and all who were present, seeking in blazing zeal from his depths what is for their edification and their eternal glory.

32.17.4.en: The three friends fell silent and found no word to utter, because they had emptied out the words that issued from their envy of Job, and became like those who have emptied what was in their quiver; but Elihu, who was silent for a time, had within him words of love that are not emptied. He wished to speak, not as one who desires to teach, nor from the seat of authority, but from the position of love and compassion for all, his words overflowing from his bowels, or as he says: "the spirit within me."

32.17.5.en: * Paul here uses a word much stronger than mere "love." For zealous souls burn with ardor toward those they love. Jealousy presupposes strong affection. Therefore, lest they suppose that Paul seeks authority, wealth or honor, he adds that his jealousy is godly. For God is said to be jealous, not in a human way, but so that each one may know his right of lordship over those whom He loves, and that what He does is for their increasing profit.

32.17.6.en: Human jealousy rests basically on selfishness, but divine jealousy is strong and pure.

32.17.7.en: Note the difference between the human bride and the Church. In the world, the virgin woman before marriage loses her virginity by her marriage. But in the Church, those who were virgins to some extent before returning to Christ enjoy virginity in Him. Therefore the whole Church is a virgin.

32.17.8.en: * God is also said to be jealous, lest anyone suppose that (the Godhead) has passion, but so that all may know that He does everything only for the sake of those over whom He is jealous, not to acquire anything but to save them.

32.17.9.en: St. John Chrysostom Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent.

32.18.0.en: It is ready to burst like new bottles [19].

32.18.1.en: Since Elihu offered an excuse for speaking in the presence of the elders, he entered into a soliloquy with himself, saying that his inside was filled with blazing zeal, so that his soul almost burst like new wineskins full of wine, or like a smith's bellows full of air. In his soliloquy he declares that he shows partiality to no one and flatters no man!

32.18.2.en: Elihu's speeches came not as one seeking an answer to questions or to accusations, but as one looking at the problem with a general view, to prepare the way for the dialogue between God and Job.

32.18.3.en: We can interpret Elihu's words symbolically: the belly indicates the depths of the heart, and the new wine the Spirit, as the Lord Christ's saying that new wine is put into new bottles (Mt 9:17). For when the disciples were filled with the Holy Spirit who came down upon them on the day of Pentecost, they became like new bottles filled with new wine, and their tongues were loosed to speak as the Spirit gave them utterance. And since the Jews did not grasp the divine truth, they accused the disciples of being full of new wine, like drunkards (Acts 2:4).

32.18.4.en: I will speak, that I may be refreshed.

32.19.0.en: I will open my lips and answer [20].

32.19.1.en: Elihu could not keep silence, so he burst out in speech that his soul might find rest. This is what happened with the prophet Jeremiah, who was filled with intense compassion toward the people of God; how he longed to be silent, but the fires of his love and the flame of the word of God in his depths compelled him to speak.

32.19.2.en: I do not think we blame Elihu for his position; rather we learn from him when to be silent and when to speak, as the wise man says: "A time to keep silence, and a time to speak" (Eccl 3:7).

32.19.3.en: * The wise man is the one who strives to please God and is much given to silence, and if he speaks, he speaks little, uttering what is necessary and pleasing to God.

32.19.4.en: * In silence you see your mind, but when you use your mind you are speaking within yourself. For during silence the mind gives birth to the word, and the word of thanksgiving offered to God is the salvation of man.

32.19.5.en: * He who speaks foolishly has no mind, for he speaks without thinking about all matters. Therefore examine what is profitable to you, for the sake of your soul's salvation, so that you may do it.

32.20.0.en: St. Abba Anthony the Great Let me not accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles (flatter) unto man [21].

32.20.1.en: It is as though he says: "I beseech you, let me not show partiality to a man for his person, nor flatter people for their titles." This is not speech addressed to those present, nor a prayer offered to God, but an expression revealing the determination of his heart to speak with the spirit of truth, without respect of persons and without flattering anyone, whatever his position or abilities. He wishes to utter the truth without fear, courtesy or personal gain for himself.

32.20.2.en: "These things also belong to the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment" (Prov 24:23).

32.20.3.en: "To have respect of persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress" (Prov 28:21).

32.20.4.en: "And, ye masters, do the same things unto them, forbearing threatening: knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him" (Eph 6:9).

32.20.5.en: "But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons" (Col 3:25).

32.20.6.en: "I charge thee before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality (1 Tim 5:21).

32.20.7.en: "My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons" (Jas 2:1).

32.20.8.en: "And if ye call on the Father, who without respect of persons judgeth according to every man's work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear" (1 Pet 1:17).

32.20.9.en: "For there is no respect of persons with God" (Rom 2:11).

32.20.10.en: "For there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts" (2 Chr 19:7).

32.20.11.en: Since God sent His only-begotten Son out of His love for the whole world, without partiality, and gave Him up for all of us, we perceive God's lack of partiality. And since we are members in the body of Christ, the Lover of mankind, it is fitting for us to have no partiality. Concerning God's lack of partiality it is said:

32.20.12.en: * God has no partiality toward persons; He judges by works.

32.20.13.en: St. John Chrysostom * If anyone doubts this, it is enough for him to read what Peter said when he visited the Gentile Cornelius: "Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: but in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him" (Acts 10:34-35). We go further than this and quote what our Lord says in the Gospel: [He that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God] (Jn 3:18).

32.20.14.en: Origen * All of us were born equal, emperors and paupers, and we die equal. Our humanity is equal.

32.20.15.en: St. Jerome Solomon the Wise himself offers us a living example of lack of partiality, as he looks upon himself, a king of great wealth and honor, as no different in anything from any pauper.

32.20.16.en: [I myself also am a mortal man, like to all, and the offspring of him that was first made of the earth, and in my mother's womb was fashioned to be flesh in the time of ten months, being compacted in blood, of the seed of man, and the pleasure that came with sleep] (Wis 7:1-2).

32.20.17.en: For I know not to give flattering titles (flattery).

32.21.0.en: In so doing my maker would soon take me away [22].

32.21.1.en: His defense of Job did not issue from partiality or flattery, nor to seek some profit for himself, for Job no longer had any authority or resources for Elihu to flatter him; rather he defends one who is in the midst of the dunghill, even if in his defense he points to the error of Job who, with his righteousness, when accused was wholly occupied with defending himself, even at the expense of affirming God's care for him and His compassion toward him.

32.21.2.en: Elihu enjoyed the sense of the divine presence, so he feared no man, a thing in whose snare many fall, as the wise man says: "The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe" (Prov 29:25). What occupied Elihu's heart was his sense of the swiftness of the Lord's coming, when he would be taken from this world and stand before Him, and give an account of all that was in his heart and thought as well as of his conduct, before the Creator who knows all the secrets of man, and from whom nothing is hidden.

32.21.3.en: This is what impelled him to silence, to listen and study with deliberation, and it is what impelled him to speak, to present the truth in simplicity and without embellishment.

32.21.4.en: Here he calls God "my maker," for He is God the Creator who is personally concerned for him and who knows his depths. He is the God of truth, and He is love; He gives the truth to His believers, reveals it to them more and more, and upholds them to speak the truth and to walk in it.

32.21.5.en: So Elihu concludes the introduction of his long speech by affirming that he flatters no one and shows no partiality to those with titles, but presents the truth in simplicity for the sake of his Maker, before whom he stands on the great day of the Lord.

32.21.6.en: Let my heart be kindled with the fire of Your word, that I may speak Your truth!

32.21.7.en: * My God, You who gave me thought and tongue!

32.21.8.en: Sanctify my depths, my words and my actions.

32.21.9.en: Let me know how to keep silent with my tongue, so that my heart speaks with love for You and for all mankind.

32.21.10.en: Let my soul groan with the groans of every heart.

32.21.11.en: And let my depths cry out with the cries of every wronged one.

32.21.12.en: Hear the cries of my soul rising to Your throne!

32.21.13.en: * Grant me to speak at a good time, to utter what You give me of words, so that I fear no man, nor flatter a rich man or one in authority.

32.21.14.en: Grant me the wisdom that sits by Your throne, so that I speak Your word, kept by Your wisdom.

32.21.15.en: * You gave me a breath from You, that I may receive Your wisdom and walk by Your Holy Spirit.

32.21.16.en: I am jealous for the salvation of every soul, and I long for You to be glorified in every man, yet in my zeal I do not rely on my bare experience, nor do the years of my life concern me, however long or short.

32.21.17.en: Rather I carry You within me, that You may speak through me, and work by Your Spirit in me and in my brethren!

32.21.18.en: Who can renew my life but You?

32.21.19.en: Who can set right the mind of my brethren except Your Spirit?

32.21.20.en: * My depths groan for every wandering soul, my bowels pain me, my heart has melted like wax for all mankind!

32.21.21.en: Let me speak, but rather You speak in me and through me.

32.21.22.en: Let me utter Your word, and my soul will rest and be comforted in You!

32.21.23.en: Let me speak, awaiting my departure to You!

32.21.24.en: Let me enter into the divine embrace, and let my soul rejoice for all those who enjoy the glories!

32.21.26.en: Come, to carry every believer to Your glories!

32.21.27.en: Our hearts will not cease to long for Your coming!
